title: Active on Facebook and Failing at School? Meta-Analytic Findings on the Relationship Between Online Social Networking Activities and Academic Achievement

RQ2.answer: The meta-analysis found that general social networking site (SNS) use and SNS use related to multitasking were negatively associated with academic achievement (grades/GPA), although the effects were small. Conversely, SNS use specifically for academic purposes showed a small positive association with academic achievement. The study found no significant relationship between general SNS use and time spent studying.

supporting_quotes.quote: The meta-analyses identified small negative effects of ρ^ = − .07, 95% CI [− .12, − .02] for general SNS use and ρ^ = − .10, 95% CI [− .16, − .05] for SNS use related to multitasking.
SNS use for academic purposes exhibited a small positive association, ρ^ = .08, 95% CI [.02, .14].
General SNS use was unrelated to the time spent studying (ρ^ = − .03, 95% CI [− 0.11, 0.06])
